featured_1_material: High-fired porcelain with underglaze cobalt-blue painting; transparent glaze; dragon roundel motif.
featured_1_condition:
Overall grade: Excellent
No visible cracks or hairlines; minor age wear to rim/foot; cobalt painting remains crisp.
featured_1_description: Imperial-quality blue-and-white vases from this period are scarce and highly collected.
featured_1_historical_background: Kangxi–Qianlong era kilns refined cobalt and firing control, making luminous blues and strong bodies. Dragon imagery signified imperial authority and auspicious power.
featured_1_cultural_impact: Inspired Delftware and Meissen; remains a global icon of Chinese craftsmanship and museum centerpiece.
featured_1_cultural_context: Likely displayed in elite or imperial interiors, signaling rank and scholarly refinement.
featured_1_care_tip:
Handle by the body/base, not rim/neck.

Dust with microfiber; avoid abrasives.

Avoid immersion; if needed, wipe with distilled water and dry.

Keep away from direct sun and rapid climate changes.

Display on padded, stable surface (museum gel if needed).
featured_2_summary: Rare Victorian era emerald and gold ring
featured_2_material: 18k gold mount with natural emerald (oval), likely closed-back or foil-back typical of the era; delicate scrollwork shoulders.
featured_2_condition:
Overall grade: Very Good
Light wear to gold; stone secure; facet junctions show mild age wear under magnification.
featured_2_description: High-grade emerald examples with original mounts are sought after, though not ultra-rare.
featured_2_historical_background: Victorian jewelry favored symbolic gems; emerald signified renewal and status. Industrial advances broadened access yet fine handwork remained prized.
featured_2_cultural_impact: Served as love tokens and markers of social standing; continues to anchor antique jewelry collections.
featured_2_cultural_context: Likely owned by upper-middle-class or aristocratic patrons; worn on formal occasions and passed as heirlooms.
featured_2_care_tip:
Keep away from heat/chemicals (emeralds often oiled).

Clean with soft dry cloth—no ultrasonic/steam.

Store separately in padded box.

Have settings checked periodically.

Avoid hard knocks; emeralds can cleave.
featured_3_material: Steel blade; gilt bronze/hilt with ornate guard; leather/scabbard fittings where present.
featured_3_condition:
Overall grade: Very Good
Light tarnish and expected age patina; engravings and gilding remain clear; fittings sound.
featured_3_description: Documented Napoleonic ceremonial arms are rare and command major premiums.
featured_3_historical_background: Presentation/ceremonial swords signified command and prestige across Napoleonic campaigns and court ceremonies.
featured_3_cultural_impact: Objects tied to Napoleon embody themes of power and statecraft; top museum and auction highlights.
featured_3_cultural_context: Commissioned for high-rank ceremonies; displayed in salons or arsenals as symbols of honor.
featured_3_care_tip:
Store in low-humidity case.

Handle with cotton/nitrile gloves.

Light oil on blade (acid-free) if conserving; avoid over-polish.

Keep gilt surfaces dry; no abrasives.

Support scabbard and hilt when moving.
featured_4_material: Stone tesserae set in mortar/plaster; avian motif panel fragment.
featured_4_condition:
Overall grade: Good
Some tesserae losses and surface wear; stable mounting; colors retain contrast.
featured_4_description: Single-panel fragments are collectible; size, subject, and preservation drive price.
featured_4_historical_background: Mosaics decorated villas, baths, and temples; subjects ranged from myth to nature. Craft guilds perfected durable floors and walls.
featured_4_cultural_impact: Became hallmarks of Roman domestic culture and luxury; informed Renaissance and modern restorations of classical taste.
featured_4_cultural_context: Likely installed in a wealthy domus or bath complex; served both decorative and symbolic purposes.
featured_4_care_tip:
Keep in stable, low-humidity environment.

Avoid water cleaning—dry dust only.

Support from beneath; do not flex panel.

Protect edges; no pressure on loose tesserae.

Professional conservation for consolidation/grout work.
